Working on ligand 1 again. Every productive link I have built puts the azine nitrogen immediately adjacent to the bridging NH - pyridin-2-ylamino and pyrimidin-2-ylamino both do - which means the NH and the ring N form a coplanar donor/acceptor pair, the classic kinase hinge arrangement. I have never tested moving that nitrogen away, and the answer changes how I design every future molecule: if adjacency is required, the 2-amino regiochemistry is non-negotiable, and if it is not, then any pyridine isomer will do and I have far more positions to decorate. Atom 6 is the aromatic carbon bearing the arylamine at atom 7, a non-ring bond, so I cut it and attach pyridin-3-ylamino instead - same atom count, same donor, same monocyclic azine, with the ring nitrogen moved from ortho to meta relative to the NH. Nothing else about the molecule changes.

The swap is clean and SA actually improved to 1.59, but LogP jumped to 4.08 because the pyridine nitrogen moved out of conjugation with the NH - which is itself a hint that the ortho arrangement was doing electronic work. QED is 0.761, again held down by the benzoyl. Atom 1 is the amide carbonyl and atom 16 is the ipso carbon of that phenyl, a non-ring bond, so I replace the ring with a methyl. The product is N-[4-(pyridin-3-ylamino)phenyl]acetamide at ~227 Da with LogP near 2.5, two aromatic rings and SA around 1.55. That makes it exactly matched to the pyridin-2-ylamino acetanilide I built earlier - same scaffold, same cap, same size, only the ring nitrogen position differs - so the pair isolates the regiochemistry question cleanly.
